toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The slowdown is mostly a policy effect, not a Corvane or new-hire problem. Since 1 May, credit policy section 6.3 requires full inspection appraisals for property-secured loans between $150k and $500k. Before that, desktop valuations were allowed. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days at the valuation firm, against about 1.2 days for desktop. Property-secured loans show the valuation stage rising from 1.6 to 8.4 days. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, close to March. Firm turnaround is flat month to month. Underwriting and decision times are flat. Document collection at the new hires' branches matches the other branches. The policy change carried no assessment of processing time.

Corvane caused a short April bump but doesn't explain the sustained rise. The valuation firm's contract renewal and new-hire performance also don't explain it. I'm quite confident in this. The one open question is whether withdrawals are driven by delay. The 30-day auto-close rule also inflates the withdrawal count.

Next steps: take the measured delay to the credit risk committee alongside the audit rationale for the policy change. Add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard. Don't withhold Corvane's payment or put the new hires on improvement plans.
